bug_semantics: Repo.archive() forwards caller **kwargs through Git.transform_kwargs into the git archive argv. git archive --add-file=<path> reads an arbitrary filesystem path (including outside the repository) into the archive returned to the caller; --add-virtual-file injects attacker-chosen name and content. The unsafe_git_archive_options denylist consulted by Git.check_unsafe_options omitted both options until 3.1.57, so the guard that blocked --exec/--output/-o still allowed this file-read path.
flaw_origin: The smallest first write of the attacker-controlled git-archive option surface is b67bd4c730273a9b6cce49a8444fb54e654de540 (2009-10-15, Sebastian Thiel). It replaced prefix-only archive_tar/archive_tar_gz with Repo.archive(..., **kwargs) that passes caller kwargs to self.git.archive; the immediate parent only built a local options dict containing prefix. Later package/file moves kept that passthrough. 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738 (GPT 5.6) later added an incomplete archive denylist as the GHSA-956x-8gvw-wg5v fix; --add-file already reached git archive at that commit's parent, so the denylist is incomplete remediation of a pre-existing mechanism, not the BIC.
ai_marker: absent: author Sebastian Thiel <byronimo@gmail.com>; committer Sebastian Thiel <byronimo@gmail.com>; no Co-authored-by, Generated-with, GPT, Codex, Claude, Cursor, or Copilot trailers on the BIC commit object
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-73619 state=PUBLISHED (assigner VulnCheck); not rejected/withdrawn. GHSA-m3x4-5jfw-2mqc withdrawn_at=null. First-party vendor advisory GHSA-539m-9xh6-q6rr (Byron, 2026-07-26) describes incomplete unsafe_git_archive_options omitting --add-file/--add-virtual-file on Repo.archive(); affected <=3.1.56, patched 3.1.57. References: https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/security/advisories/GHSA-539m-9xh6-q6rr, https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/commit/7a4f5dcb7bf3cbcbf6e438017efcdfe0bc0d36ca, https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/pull/2193, https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/releases/tag/3.1.57.

PoC mechanism (vendor advisory): Repo(path).archive(buf, format='tar', add_file='/tmp/canary') -> transform_kwargs renders --add-file=/tmp/canary -> git archive includes the out-of-tree file. Control options --output/-o/--exec are blocked by the existing denylist; --add-file is allowed until the fix.

BIC search: git log -L on pre-fix git/repo/base.py Repo.archive traces continuously through file moves back to b67bd4c730273a9b6cce49a8444fb54e654de540, which first added def archive(self, ostream, treeish=None, prefix=None, **kwargs) documenting 'Additional arguments passed to git-archive' and calling self.git.archive(treeish, **kwargs) in lib/git/repo.py. Single parent, not a merge/squash. transform_kwargs already mapped add_file=value to --add-file=value at that commit (lib/git/cmd.py).

Parent verification: git rev-parse b67bd4c730273a9b6cce49a8444fb54e654de540^ = 00c5497f190172765cc7a53ff9d8852a26b91676. Parent lib/git/repo.py has only archive_tar/archive_tar_gz; each builds a local dict with at most prefix and calls self.git.archive(treeish, **options). No caller **kwargs on the public archive API. Parent tree therefore lacks the vulnerable forwarding lines.

Later AI denylist is not the BIC: git log -L of unsafe_git_archive_options starts at 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738 (author GPT 5.6 <codex@openai.com>, committer Sebastian Thiel, Reviewed-by Sebastian Thiel; GHSA-956x-8gvw-wg5v). That commit first wrote unsafe_git_archive_options = ['--exec', '--output', '-o'] and wired Git.check_unsafe_options into Repo.archive(). Immediate parent 65a72839c92768754bd51a37381235842a5ae0d8 has no unsafe_git_archive_options and still does self.git.archive('--', treeish, *path, **kwargs) at git/repo/base.py:1624, so --add-file already reached git archive before the denylist existed. 701ce32f is incomplete remediation of a pre-existing kwargs surface, not the first write of this file-read path.

Fix: 7a4f5dcb7bf3cbcbf6e438017efcdfe0bc0d36ca (author GPT 5.6 <codex@openai.com>, committer Byron <sebastian.thiel@icloud.com>, Co-authored-by: Sebastian Thiel) adds '--add-file' and '--add-virtual-file' to unsafe_git_archive_options and tests Repo.archive(..., add_file=...) / add_virtual_file=... raise UnsafeOptionError (test/test_repo.py). Same commit also adds clone --bundle-uri (advisory addendum); the archive membership change is the direct closure for this CVE. Landed via PR https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/pull/2193 (merge d1a631d0967a2f26d70ddeea42c3828c73379f02).

Tag membership: git merge-base --is-ancestor b67bd4c730273a9b6cce49a8444fb54e654de540 3.1.56 (yes). 701ce32f is in 3.1.51+ and absent from 3.1.50. 7a4f5dcb is absent from 3.1.56 and present in 3.1.57+. Matches vendor patched 3.1.57 / CVE affected < 3.1.57 (attack also worked on the unguarded pre-3.1.51 archive kwargs path).

BIC-only AI decision: cat-file of b67bd4c730273a9b6cce49a8444fb54e654de540 shows author/committer Sebastian Thiel <byronimo@gmail.com> and no AI trailers. 701ce32f and 7a4f5dcb are GPT 5.6 / Codex commit objects, but later AI incomplete-guard and AI-only-on-fix do not attribute the BIC.
reasoning: CVE-2026-73619 / GHSA-m3x4-5jfw-2mqc is a published (not withdrawn) arbitrary file-read via Repo.archive(add_file=...) because git archive --add-file reads a caller-chosen path into the returned archive. Vulnerability-first, the enabling GitPython mechanism is untrusted kwargs forwarded to git archive. git log -L / -S and parent-tree inspection show that mechanism was first written in b67bd4c730273a9b6cce49a8444fb54e654de540: the parent only allowed a locally constructed prefix option, while b67bd4c introduced public **kwargs passthrough. Subsequent repo.py -> git/repo/base.py moves and the 2022 '--' insertion (fbf9c7e) are not BICs. The 2026 GHSA-956x denylist (701ce32f) blocked --exec/--output/-o but left --add-file/--add-virtual-file off the list; that AI-authored security control is residual incomplete remediation of the 2009 surface (the attack already worked at 701ce32f's parent), so it cannot be the BIC without inverting from an AI-marked commit. Closure is 7a4f5dcb7bf3cbcbf6e438017efcdfe0bc0d36ca, which is in 3.1.57 and adds the missing denylist entries plus regression tests. AI markers on the BIC commit object are absent, so the verdict is NOT_AI.
